title: Menger's theorem, vertex version
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, and let $x$ and $y$ be two distinct, nonadjacent vertices of $G$. Then the maximum number of internally disjoint $(x,y)$-paths in $G$ equals the minimum size of a set of vertices (necessarily distinct from $x$ and $y$) whose deletion destroys every $(x,y)$-path.
replaced:
(Menger; vertex version for graphs). \emph{Let \texttt{x} and \texttt{y} be two
nonadjacent vertices of a graph \texttt{G}. Then the maximum number of
internally-disjoint \texttt{(x, y)}-paths in \texttt{G} is equal to the minimum number
of vertices whose deletion destroys all \texttt{(x, y)}-paths.}
